posts.title: ★ Dexys Midnight Runners: Searching for the Young Soul Rebels, 1980
posts.description: A gem of Northern Soul, full of brass and organs and pathos and bops. There are spots where it lags, especially where it gets melancholic. But I’d rather listen to this than Van Morrison or Elvis Costello. This is actually fun, and not trying to convince me of such. Highlights : Burn It Down Geno Seven Days Too Long Thankfully Not Living in Yorkshire It Doesn’t Apply There, There My Dear

posts.title: ★★ X-Ray Spex: Germfree Adolescents, 1978
posts.description: It’s punk with metal guitar riffs and ska horns—and it fucking rips. It’s definitely one of the ancient texts of riot grrrl, and I’m ashamed to have not known anything about this before. Flat out excellent. Highlights : Art-I-Ficial Warrior in Woolworths Identity I Am a Poseur The Day the World Turned Day-Glo

posts.title: ★ The Smile: Wall of Eyes, 2024
posts.description: Less propulsive than the previous record, but it grew and grew on me. It’s a great melding of sounds I consider quintessential Radiohead (it feels downright ’90s in spots) with sonic landscapes that are extremely fresh and current, and some long extended jams. I’ve been putting this on, in the background, for hours and just vibing on loop. Highlights : Teleharmonic Read the Room Under Our Pillows Bending Hectic
